```text
BOUNDARY: The definitions are stated for an arbitrary ordered field F; no
completeness or Archimedean hypothesis is assumed.  The uniqueness-of-limits
argument in the Remarks uses only the unordered‑field properties of the
absolute value ([[lem-of-abs-value]]), the triangle inequality
([[lem-of-triangle-inequality]]), and the fact that 2 = 1+1 > 0 in any
ordered field; the argument is valid without further restrictions.  The
example with ℝ((t⁻¹)) in the Remarks correctly illustrates that restricting
ε to the canonical rationals in a non‑Archimedean field changes the meaning
of convergence/Cauchy, and the reasoning is supported by clause 4 of
[[lem-laurent-non-archimedean]] (the constant term is non‑zero at index 0,
so a positive constant exceeds t⁻¹).  All degenerate cases (constant
sequences, eventually zero lengths, intervals with a=b) are handled
consistently by the given definitions.  No counterexample to any claimed
property was found.
```
